message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.17","text":"I also set out the purpose I had from the beginning, how I had exhausted myself in inquiries with no way through, and everything I disclosed to you at the outset, so that I need not write the same things again. I said, “I am quite ready to accompany you—for I do not know how it is that I gladly desire this. Yet I first want to be fully assured about the truth, so that I may know whether the soul happens to be mortal or is immortal; and, if it is eternal, whether it is to be judged for what it has done here; whether there is, after all, anything just or pleasing to God; whether the world has come into being and why it came into being; whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved; and whether it will be better or will not even exist. And, not to speak of each matter category by category, I said that I wanted to learn these things and what follows from them.” He answered this: “In brief, Clement, I will provide you with knowledge of what exists; for now, hear from it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς ζητήσεις ἀπόρους ἐκενώθην","chosen":"I had exhausted myself in inquiries with no way through","rationale":"Preserves the imagery of being emptied or spent while expressing ἀπόρους as inquiries offering no path to a solution."},{"source_quote":"πληροφορηθῆναι","chosen":"to be fully assured","rationale":"Conveys complete conviction or assurance rather than merely receiving information."},{"source_quote":"εἰ οὐ λυθήσεται καὶ εἰ λυθήσεται","chosen":"whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved","rationale":"Retains both explicitly stated alternatives and does not remove the first negation as redundant."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾿ εἶδος λέγω","chosen":"not to speak of each matter category by category","rationale":"Κατ᾿ εἶδος indicates treating the questions individually according to their kinds."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τῶν ὄντων γνῶσιν","chosen":"knowledge of what exists","rationale":"Renders the philosophical expression τὰ ὄντα without importing a more specialized metaphysical term."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.18","text":"The counsel of God has become hidden in many ways. First come bad initiation, wicked nurture, harsh habituation, unwholesome company, and incorrect preconception. From these come error, then absence of fear, unbelief, sexual immorality, love of money, vainglory, and countless other such evils. Like a mass of smoke, these inhabited the world as a single house and, after clouding the sight of the people dwelling inside, did not allow them to look up from the delineation, discern the God who created it, and recognize what seems good to him. Therefore lovers of truth must cry out from deep within their breasts and summon help by truth-loving reasoning, so that someone outside the smoke-filled house may approach and open a door, in order that the sunlight outside may be admitted into the house and the smoke inside, arising from the fire, may be expelled.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰσαγωγὴ κακή, συντροφία πονηρά, συνήθεια δεινή, ὁμιλία οὐ καλή, πρόληψις οὐκ ὀρθή","chosen":"bad initiation, wicked nurture, harsh habituation, unwholesome company, and incorrect preconception","rationale":"Distinguishes initial formation, upbringing, acquired habit, social association, and prior assumption rather than flattening them into one kind of influence."},{"source_quote":"ἀφοβία","chosen":"absence of fear","rationale":"Avoids the positive connotations of English “fearlessness” while not adding an object such as God that the Greek leaves unstated."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἕνα οἶκον οἰκοῦντα τὸν κόσμον","chosen":"inhabited the world as a single house","rationale":"Keeps the image of the evils or smoke occupying the whole world as though it were one house."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ τῆς διαγραφῆς","chosen":"from the delineation","rationale":"Διαγραφή presents the visible order as an outlined design from which one might look toward its maker."},{"source_quote":"φιλαλήθει λογισμῷ","chosen":"by truth-loving reasoning","rationale":"Preserves the repeated φιλαλήθης language and the cognitive force of λογισμός."},{"source_quote":"εἰσκριθῆναι τῷ οἴκῳ","chosen":"may be admitted into the house","rationale":"The passive verb depicts the outside light being allowed or brought into the house."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.19","text":"By the man who helps, then, I mean the true prophet, who alone can illuminate human souls, so that we may be able to see with our own eyes the road of eternal salvation. Otherwise this is impossible, as you yourself know, since you said a little earlier that every thesis is refuted and established and that, depending on the ability of the person defending it, the same thesis is regarded as true and false. Thus theses no longer appear as what they are but, because of those who defend them, take on the appearance of being or not being true or false. Because of this, the whole enterprise of piety required a true prophet, so that he might tell us realities as they are and how one must believe about everything. Accordingly, one must first test the prophet by every prophetic examination and recognize him as true; from then on, one must believe him in everything and no longer examine individually each thing said by him, but receive those things as certain—apparently by faith, yet accepted on the basis of sure judgment. For through one demonstration—the exact examination made at the beginning from every side—everything has been grasped correctly by sound reasoning. Therefore, before everything else, one must seek the true prophet, because without him it is impossible for human beings to have anything certain.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸν βοηθὸν ἄνδρα","chosen":"the man who helps","rationale":"Retains both the personal noun ἄνδρα and the assisting function expressed by βοηθόν."},{"source_quote":"μικρῷ τάχιον εἰπὼν","chosen":"since you said a little earlier","rationale":"In this temporal expression τάχιον means “earlier”; the participle agrees with the addressed Clement."},{"source_quote":"πᾶσα ὑπόθεσις ἀνασκευάζεται καὶ κατασκευάζεται","chosen":"every thesis is refuted and established","rationale":"Uses the paired argumentative senses of ἀνασκευάζω and κατασκευάζω and treats ὑπόθεσις as a proposition under debate."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν τοῦ ἐκδικοῦντος δύναμιν","chosen":"depending on the ability of the person defending it","rationale":"Here ἐκδικέω concerns advocating or defending a case, not taking vengeance."},{"source_quote":"δοκούσῃ μὲν πίστει, ληφθέντα δὲ ἀσφαλεῖ κρίσει","chosen":"apparently by faith, yet accepted on the basis of sure judgment","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between the apparent mode of acceptance and the prior secure evaluation of the prophet."},{"source_quote":"βέβαιόν τι προσεῖναι ἀνθρώποις","chosen":"for human beings to have anything certain","rationale":"Expresses προσεῖναι as something securely present or available to people rather than as a physical addition."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.20","text":"And in like manner he set my mind at rest, laying out for me who he is and how he may be found, and making him truly findable to me. Through the discussion of the prophet he showed the truth to my ears more plainly than things seen with the eyes, so that, struck with amazement, I marveled at how no one perceives the things everyone seeks, though they lie before them. But once I had written the discourse about the prophet at his command, he had the volume sent to you from Caesarea of Strato, saying that he had received from you a command to write down and send you, year by year, the discourses and deeds. Nevertheless, on that very first day, while still only making a beginning concerning the prophet of truth, he fully assured me about everything. Then he said: “From now on, look closely at the debates I conduct with those on the opposing side. If I come off worse, I am not afraid that you might waver over the truth handed down to you, knowing that it was I who appeared to be defeated, not the thesis handed down to us through the prophet. Yet I hope not to have come off worse even in the discourse of examination, in the judgment of those who have understanding—I mean lovers of truth—who can recognize which arguments are persuasive, skillfully fashioned, and pleasing, and which are plain and simple, relying solely on the truth conveyed through them.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς ἀνέπαυσέν με","chosen":"And in like manner he set my mind at rest","rationale":"Treats the supplied ὁμῶς as an adverb of likeness and renders ἀναπαύω idiomatically while preserving its sense of relief."},{"source_quote":"τῇ τοῦ προφήτου ὁμιλίᾳ","chosen":"Through the discussion of the prophet","rationale":"The surrounding references to a discourse about the prophet support taking the genitive objectively; “through the prophet’s discourse” remains grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"οὐδεὶς ἐνορᾷ","chosen":"no one perceives","rationale":"Ἐνοράω denotes seeing into or discerning, not merely receiving a visual impression."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἧττον ἀπενέγκωμαι","chosen":"I come off worse","rationale":"Renders the idiom of carrying away the lesser result in a contest or debate."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς παραδοθείσης σοι ἀληθείας διακριθήσῃ","chosen":"you might waver over the truth handed down to you","rationale":"In this context διακρίνω describes doubt or inward hesitation rather than analytical distinction."},{"source_quote":"ἐν τῷ ἐξεταστικῷ λόγῳ","chosen":"in the discourse of examination","rationale":"Keeps the explicit connection with testing or critical inquiry rather than reducing λόγος to casual conversation."},{"source_quote":"πιθανοὶ ἔντεχνοί τε καὶ ἐπιτερπεῖς","chosen":"persuasive, skillfully fashioned, and pleasing","rationale":"Preserves the three distinct qualities attributed to rhetorically effective arguments."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"πλὴν γράψας τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","issue":"The nominative participle γράψας would normally share the subject of ἐποίησεν, making the same man both write the discourse and act at another man’s command. The context instead indicates that Clement wrote at the command of the man who then caused the volume to be sent. The translation follows that contextual sense, but the supplied syntax has an unresolved subject clash.","proposed_reading":"πλὴν γράψαντός μου τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
